title: Atollo — Portable Dev & AI Workspace, a microVM for every project
description: The portable configurator of Docker Sandboxes: every project in its own microVM, with an editor, 20+ languages, local databases, local AI models and the Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Pi agents, in one folder. Windows x64, macOS on Apple silicon, Linux x64 and ARM64. Zero install, zero admin rights.
heroTitle: Every project in its own microVM, all in one folder.
heroLead: The portable configurator of Docker Sandboxes: editor, runtimes, databases and AI agents, with each project's code sealed in a microVM. On Windows, macOS and Linux.
heroZero: Zero install. Zero admin rights. Sandboxes, disks and settings stay in your Atollo folder.
statTargets: systems and architectures from the same folder, the ones Docker Sandboxes runs on: Windows x64, macOS on Apple silicon, Linux x64 and ARM64
statComponents: languages, tools and servers in the catalog
statAgents: AI agents with a single configuration
ctaText: One file, one empty folder. The rest arrives when needed.
noRelease: No release published yet: the files arrive with the first tag.
f1Text: Atollo configures Docker Sandboxes for you: each project runs in a microVM of its own, with its own Linux kernel. Terminal, actions, the project's website (a container in the VM), Claude Code and Codex all live there and see only the project's folder, with the kit's tools for Linux mounted read-only. The kit's terminals open in a microVM per folder. Databases stay on the PC: the VM reaches only their port, as the project's user. Where the VM cannot start, everything runs on the PC in a sealed environment, and the status bar says why and how to fix it. The editor is the built-in VSCodium, with the Atollo dark and light themes.
f2Text: 20+ languages and tools (Node.js, Python, uv, PHP, Rust, Go, Java, .NET, Dart, Julia, Ruby, C/C++, Bun, Deno, Typst, TinyTeX, R, Android SDK…), downloaded when needed and verified by SHA-256 checksum or signature. Side-by-side versions, one per project.
f3Text: MySQL with phpMyAdmin, MongoDB with mongo-express, and SQLite, started and stopped with one click, with a database, user and password for each project; several versions side by side, each keeping its own port. The servers stay on the PC, and a project's VM reaches only its own database. Caddy and Apache for sites at .localhost addresses, on every system, on their own or in a server shared by several projects; in the VM a project's site runs as a container on localhost. A port already in use is refused, naming whoever holds it. No system services.
f4Text: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and Pi: install, sign in and start; with the VM on, Claude Code and Codex run in Docker Sandboxes' agent sandboxes (Antigravity and Pi only without it). Write instructions, skills and MCP servers once in data/agents and atollo sync keeps all four aligned. Plan limits and usage for today and the last 7 days. Local models too, with no network and no account: GGUF models from Atollo's catalog or Hugging Face, resumable downloads checked by SHA-256, a llama.cpp server on 127.0.0.1 with a key that Pi uses out of the box.
f5Text: The same folder, or the same external SSD, moves from Windows to macOS to Linux with projects, databases and agent settings intact: each machine runs the native programs of its system. “Remove drive” closes everything Atollo opened and lets you eject the disk.
how1: Copy Atollo into an empty folder: a USB stick, an external drive or a folder in your profile.
how2: Start it: it creates projects/ and data/. On first start choose agents, languages and tools; Atollo downloads and verifies them, Docker Sandboxes included. Then sign in to Docker (a free account) with sbx login in Atollo's terminal: the “No VM” notice in the status bar opens it for you.
how3: Create a project from one of 60+ bases (Laravel, Next.js, Django, WordPress, Astro, Tauri…), clone it from GitHub or start from an empty folder. The terminal, actions and agents always open in the project's folder, inside its microVM when the PC allows it.
a1Title: A microVM per project, native programs for the kit
a1Text: A project's code runs in a Docker Sandboxes microVM: its own kernel, only its folder, the network through the sandbox proxy, and the GitHub token, when you allow it for a project, added by the proxy without ever entering the VM. The kit's own programs (database servers, editor, Git, Docker Sandboxes itself) are native on each system. Atollo needs no administrator rights, installs no services and never touches the system registry or PATH; the hypervisor is the one thing you turn on yourself, once. It starts from a USB stick or an external SSD too.
a2Text: Projects, AI (agents and local models), databases, web servers, terminals, tools and settings each have their own page. The Projects quick panel shows what is running, your favourites and what needs fixing, and Ctrl+P opens a project by name; the Activity panel gathers in one place the output and errors of whatever is running or installing, from project actions to every database version and web server pool, and “Stop all” stops it all after a confirmation. For scripts there is the command line: atollo check, atollo prepare, atollo sync.
a3Text: When the drive letter, the folder or the system changes, Atollo realigns the paths and on each system uses that system's programs. Projects, databases, sign-ins, agent settings and the VMs' disks stay as they were; the Docker sign-in is done once per PC.
a4Text: Every download is checked against its SHA-256 checksum or signature before it is used. A language's versions sit side by side, one per project, and the relations matrix warns when two components don't get along.
toolsLead: Every component in Atollo's catalog, by kind, on each of the four systems. Only the ones you choose are downloaded, or when a project needs them. The table is generated from the app's catalog every time the site is published.
mxLegendNo: not available (hover the cell for the reason)

platformsLead: Windows 10 and 11 on x64, macOS 12 or later on Apple silicon, Linux x64 and ARM64 with glibc 2.35 or later (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12 and newer): the systems Docker builds Docker Sandboxes for. The projects' microVM needs 64-bit Windows 11 with Windows Hypervisor Platform, a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 14, or Ubuntu 24.04 with KVM, plus a free Docker account; elsewhere the projects run on the PC.
platformsNote: On macOS the app only has an ad hoc signature: after unzipping, remove the quarantine with xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine Atollo.app and open it from the kit folder. The macOS and Linux releases are tested in CI, not yet on clean machines.
todoLead: Atollo is in alpha. Windows x64 is the most tested system, real installs in CI included; macOS and Linux are built and tested in CI only. Here is what is still missing, plainly.
t1Text: The 0.7.0 alpha is on GitHub for Windows x64, macOS on Apple silicon and Linux x64 and ARM64. The published files are built and tested in CI: now they need downloading and starting on clean machines.
t2Text: We need people using Atollo on real projects and different PCs, and reporting what goes wrong: component installs, projects, the microVMs, databases, agents.
t3Text: The Apple Silicon build is built and started in CI, never on a clean Mac: the zip downloaded with a browser, quarantine and Gatekeeper, App Translocation, a kit on an exFAT stick, the agents' sign-in carried from one Mac to another.
t4Text: x64 and ARM64 on Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 42 and Debian 13: AppImage with and without FUSE, the tar.gz with WebKitGTK 4.1, exFAT sticks or sticks mounted noexec, sign-in with GNOME, KeePassXC or KWallet.
t5Title: Updates and the kit's builds outside Windows
t5Text: Updating the app from one version to the next on macOS and Linux is not tried yet. The kit's Apache (2.4.69) is in the catalog but tried only in CI; so is the kit's PHP with pdo_sqlite (8.4.26 and 8.5.11), which the app uses from 0.3.0 on.
t6Text: On macOS only an ad hoc signature, without Apple notarization: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine is needed. On Windows 0.7.0 ships unsigned: the SignPath signature is still to be activated, and until then SmartScreen may warn on first launch.
todoHelp: Have a Mac with Apple silicon or a Linux PC? Try Atollo and tell us how it went:
privacyText: Atollo collects no data and contacts no server run by its author. It only connects to GitHub to look for its own updates, to the official sources of the components you choose, to Open VSX for the editor's extensions, to Docker for Docker Sandboxes (sign-in and the VMs' network, with its telemetry and diagnostics upload turned off) and, if you use them, to the GitHub and agent APIs.
footerSigning: Free code signing on Windows provided by SignPath.io, certificate by SignPath Foundation.
